messages:
maya: quick follow-up to the mini-cp RFC — thinking through an ops-forward rollout for a tiny control plane proxy that runs in customer VPCs. main goals: local cert verification, short-lived token minting, and minimal telemetry forwarding. thoughts?

sam: +1 we need to be explicit about what stays central vs local. can the proxy do authz checks or only token exchange?

maya: proposal: proxy handles token exchange and cert stapling only. authz decisions remain central to avoid divergent policy state. local proxy should be minimal: <100MB RAM, single binary, no DB.

zach: sounds good. what about observability? we can't stream all traces out, cost/egress will explode for big tenants.

maya: agree. plan is: metrics/health via aggregated counters (prometheus pushgateway -> central relay) and sample traces only on errors. logs buffered and batched with size cap. will throttle to avoid NAT/egress surprises.

olivia: how do we handle audit logs for regulatory customers who insist logs never leave their VPC?

maya: we support two modes: relay-to-central (default) and local-sink (customer-managed S3/forwarder). local-sink mode requires the proxy to sign and timestamp entries and expose a signed manifest to central control plane for verification.

sam: that local-sink path adds complexity. is there a way to keep trust minimal? maybe use an attestation flow: proxy signs logs with a key provisioned via KMS/HSM and central CP verifies signature without ingesting full logs.

maya: yes, attestation approach is ideal. flow sketch: 1) proxy writes logs to local sink. 2) proxy computes periodic digest and signs with customer key/hardwr KMS. 3) proxy pushes digest+signature to central control plane which verifies. central can request slices if needed under policy.

zach: rollout concerns: we can't force customers to open private peering for every tenant. should mini-cp support NATed egress with ephemeral sockets?

maya: support NAT egress + health-check windows. proxies should prefer private link when available but fall back to TLS over public egress with mTLS. we need robust backoff and queueing for token fetches to avoid thundering-herd to central.

infra-bot: deploy-bench: started a perf spike test of a minimal proxy image (v0.1-alpha) across 12 small VMs, avg mem 68MB, token-latency 45ms internal -> central in same region. logs: batch window 5s by default.

olivia: good data. one more: how do we do upgrades without breaking pinned customer routes (some have strict egress rules)?

maya: two paths: in-place rolling update with backward-compatible wire protocol, or sidecar swap with DNS/ENI switch. recommend rollout policy that prefers canary per-account and a forced-compatible-mode header during dual-mode for 2 weeks.

sam: compatibility matrix needs to include old central CP versions. we should add a compatibility test harness for each central release verifying token exchange and attestation flows.

olivia: and an ops runbook for 'proxy can't reach central' — what should app behavior be? fail open or fail closed?

maya: default: fail-open for token renewals with a short grace-window (e.g., 60s) to preserve latency-sensitive inference calls. For authz-critical operations, fail-closed. make both configurable per-tenant.

zach: one more nit: who owns cert rotation if proxy is ephemeral and customer rotates their CA?

maya: owner model: customer rotates CA; proxy watches local secret (K8s secret or local file) and performs hot reload. central CP issues validation grace period and can push warning alerts if rotation looks inconsistent.

arch-review: SYNC NOTE: prefer this design over pushing policy -> local proxies. keep policy central. add security review (HSM/KMS attest) and SRE runbook for mass-ejection scenarios.

maya: next steps: write an ops-runbook + compatibility tests, prototype attestation digest flow, and add sampling rules for telemetry. I'll draft a short RFC update with diagrams.

sam: happy to help with compatibility harness.

olivia: I'll scope the local-sink encryption requirements and customer onboarding checklist.

zach: I'll wire up the perf tests and add egress-cost estimates for NAT vs privatelink.

maya: thanks all — I'll post the RFC update in #architecture when ready. :thumbsup:
